dissent: A defender may note the done bug only fires at permuted positions; linear-prefix refusals are judged correctly—but permuted schedules are the declared domain, so the defect stands.

implement's 'not inspected' skip is defensible as honest non-inspection; it becomes a defect only when composed with run_controls' narrow detection predicate, which the shared (cases, charge) API explicitly invites.
Both modules' scoping claims (supplied cases only, no global theorem, declared journal/digest limitations) are themselves sound.
findings: control-build.py:119 `done = (before.get('done') or 0) | (1 << actions.index(action))` uses adapter['actions'], the chronological schedule, so the bit position is schedule index. The checked semantics (a_audit.py `after['done']==before['done']|(1<<profile['actions'].index(action))`; adapter_traces.py restore `sum(1<<trace['profile']['actions'].index(a) for a in executed)`) require inventory index. On any permuted schedule—the whole 192-order boundary shard—clean evidence is flagged: fixture shape, middle order attempt:3@16 executed chronologically at index 11, refused 'attempt:3:attempt-gap'; predicted bit 1<<11 vs actual 1<<16 at prefix 12. Baseline becomes 'counterexample' and every run_controls entry reports detected, including the expected-False journal-drift canary. Minimal fix: index adapter['profile']['actions'] and require 'profile' in the probe.

Structural tamper is classified inconsistently, breaking real interoperability. implement.py:117-120 routes _structure failures (e.g. dropped event → 'adapter event inventory/patch mismatch') to a 'not inspected' limitation and skips the case; the sole mutated case then reports 'not_applicable', while run_controls (control-build.py:168) counts detection only via status=='counterexample' → 'refusal-event-dropped' records detected=False. Under control-build's own inspect_cases the same bytes give an 'inventory' violation → 'counterexample' → detected=True. adapter_traces.restore treats inventory loss as hard failure. Minimal fix: record structural mismatches as counterexample, or count 'not inspected' as detected.

control-build.py:110-113 `continue`s on invoked rows after invocations-extended, skipping outer done-bit and decision==core.decision checks that a_audit.py enforces on every step (`after['done']==...`, `after['decision']==reason` where reason is the core decision); the 12-key journal frame is never checked either (a_audit.initialization/a_domain.initial). implement.py:138-141,172-196 covers all three each prefix. A healed delegated-decision launder or done-bit drop on an invoked row is invisible to control-build. Minimal fix: port implement's delegated-decision/done-bit/journal-frame checks or narrow the a_audit parity claim.

control-build.py:29-31 `import semantic as rel` transitively loads s_domain→q_domain→p_domain/p_literal and q_audit—the audit relation and fixture corpus under comparison—contradicting the 'no ... audit ... imported' inspection posture and coupling controls to the originals' import health; implement.py is import-free (_typed :42-47). Also, run_controls' inspect() collapses any exception including charge.take exhaustion into {'status':'error'} with no audited_prefixes, while make()-time exceptions (e.g. list-typed invocations `+` tuple :156) escape uncaught—precharge accounting is not failure-transparent.

summary: NEEDS_CORRECTION. Both o08 artifacts are present and were cross-reviewed against a_audit/a_domain/adapter_traces/check.py semantics. control-build has a wrong-domain done-bit index causing systematic false 'counterexample' on permuted schedules plus trivialized control discrimination; the pair are not interoperable for structural tamper; lesser coverage and independence defects noted.
